records: Every home and business in the UK has the legal right to request a decent, affordable broadband connection.
Ofcom defines a decent connection for the universal service as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Requests are made to BT, except in the Hull area where KCOM is the designated provider.
An applicant does not need to be an existing BT or KCOM customer.
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and the estimated build cost.
Eligibility requires that the home or business has no access to existing decent broadband.
Eligibility also requires that the premises will not be covered by a UK or devolved-government public broadband scheme in the next 12 months.
A premises that can only obtain a decent service priced above £59.60 per month can also request a universal service connection.
If the applicant's share of building or upgrading the connection costs £3,400 or less, the applicant does not pay for that work.
If the applicant's share costs more than £3,400, the applicant may proceed by paying the excess costs.
For an excess-cost connection, BT or KCOM will conduct a survey and provide a quote within 60 days.
The resulting broadband service is priced the same as the same package for other customers and no more than £59.60 per month.
Ofcom says most eligible applicants will receive a connection within 12 months.
Ofcom says some universal-service connections can take up to 24 months.

If an eligibility complaint remains unresolved for eight weeks, or reaches deadlock sooner, customers have free access to alternative dispute resolution and need not already be BT or KCOM customers to dispute the decision.
Ofcom's Broadband Speeds Code of Practice requires clear information about expected speeds when a broadband service is purchased.
When a provider-side network problem prevents promised speeds and is not fixed within 30 days, the customer must be offered exit without an early termination fee.
The consumer protections page lists BT, EE, NOW Broadband, Plusnet, Sky, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Zen Internet.
Speed estimates should cover busy periods: 8pm to 10pm for home services and noon to 2pm for business services.
A provider should give the customer a personalised minimum guaranteed speed.
